#3753. GTA 6′s Pop And Classic Rock Radio Stations Contain 150 Songs, More Than All Of Vice City’s Radio Stations Combined

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6MusicRockstar Games

If you haven’t heard already: Grand Theft Auto 6, finally out now on PS5 and Xbox, is a very big video game. It’s also one of the best games I’ve played in years. And one reason I love it so much is because of all the great music on the in-game radio stations. There are so many songs. In fact, just two of the game’s biggest radio stations contain more songs than all of GTA: Vice City’s radio stations combined did back on the PS2.

Two of the biggest radio stations inÂ GTA 6Â are FLASH FM, a pop station, and V-ROCK, a classic rock station. Funnily enough, both of these stations appeared in Vice City, too. But this time around, the stations have a lot more music. Let’s do some number crunching!

In GTA: Vice City‘s version of V-Rock, there were (before some songs were cut in later ports for licensing reasons) 17 songs. Meanwhile, Vice City‘s Flash FM featured 15 songs. And in total, there were 106 songs in GTA 6 across its various stations. In GTA 6, Flash FM alone now boasts 80 songs, according to Rockstar’s recently released credits. And V-Rock now has 70 songs. Combined, there are more songs on just these two stations than in all of Vice City.

After playing 150 hours of GTA 6, I’m still hearing new songs. Last night, I booted up the game and heard “Hot To Go!” for the first time, which blew me away. And I listened to these two stations a lot!

Anyway, if you’re curious about what’s playing on these two stations, here are the full lists of songs on Flash FM and V-Rock:

After considerable speculation and a plethora of reports, it was finally confirmed this week that Robert Pattinson would take on the mantle of James Bond. I personally didn’t have my money on the Batman actor trading in his cape for a suit, but I'm not mad at it! Now, additional details are starting to reach the surface, as it's been alleged that Pattinson was pulled into an audition after executives were struggling to make a decision. With that, he was allegedly paid a large sum of money to test for the role, and it seems a lot more of that green could come his way.

According to a report from The Mirror, the Dune actor received $1 million just to audition for 007. To say that's a considerable amount of money would be an understatement. However, Amazon MGM Studios has neither confirmed nor denied that total. As surreal as that sum might seem, there's more to this.

Pattinson -- who has since been congratulated by the British Royal Family and more -- the Royal Family welcomed him as the next Bond. Apparently, the Drama star has signed a three-year deal to play Commander Bond and could allegedly make somewhere between £58 million ($76 million) and £75 million ($98 million). Again, none of this is confirmed, but such a paycheck would make sense, given the deal and the sheer size of this storied IP.

Meanwhile, fans have mixed reactions to the casting news, with some already on board with seeing Pattinson’s take on 007 and others feeling like there were other prime options. A number of notable stars were in the mix before Pattinson was cast, with Jack Lowden notably emerging as a reported favorite. Some may wonder how Pattinson was decided upon and, per an insider, the process wasn't cut and dry.

Per a source for The Mirror, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' wife, Lauren Sanchez, was a major proponent of Robert Pattinson being cast in the role. Sanchez has allegedly long been a fan of the Primetime star and supposedly helped push him to the forefront when it came to Bond casting. The insider said:

Robert wasn’t the name everyone was talking about. There were other actors who seemed much further down the road. Then, suddenly, he was the man everybody wanted. Lauren’s push for him was hardly a secret in certain circles. Jeff might be the man with the billions, but Lauren has his ear.

Details on Bond 26 are being kept under wraps, including the title and premise. At this point, it also feels unlikely that it'll be released in 2027. However, we do know that Denis Villeneuve will be directing the movie, meaning this will be a Dune reunion for him and Pattinson. There is a lot of speculation surrounding who will join Pattinson, as names are being thrown out for the next Bond villain. And, of course, many are wondering who will be the next Bond girl with rumors placing Margaret Qualley in the lead as a strong candidate.

Regardless of what actually unfolds within the next 007 movie, this new report suggests that Robert Pattinson will be well compensated for the role. What's more is that this reported deal comes near the end of a year that saw him headline multiple high-profile movies. And, of course, can be seen in the upcoming Dune: Part Three, as well as 2028's The Batman: Part II. Needless to say, the man is booked and busy.

Pattinson's clearly come a long way, from playing a sparkling vampire in Twilight to playing a doomed young wizard in Harry Potter. Now, he can add being the ninth James Bond to his resume (and his bank account may be fuller for it).

If you're looking to take a break from playing GTA 6 this weekend, there are plenty of new shows and movies to get stuck into. As well as The Odyssey finally landing on digital platforms, Prime Video, Netflix, Disney Plus and Paramount Plus also have some major releases included in their subscriptions.

Among them is the final season of Yellowjackets, which finally kicks off on November 20. You'll be able to see how it all pans out in the thriller series on Paramount Plus. Speaking of returning shows, Percy Jackson and the Olympians is also back with a new season, and it has debuted to a near-perfect score on Rotten Tomatoes.

Elsewhere, Netflix has released a critically acclaimed drama led by Léa Seydoux about a concert pianist whose husband has been harboring a dark secret. Prime Video has also quietly dropped an Oscar-nominated director's latest movie without much fanfare too in the Nicolas Cage-starrer Madden. For more on all of these, read on for our guide to the best new shows and movies to stream this week.

Available: US/UKWhere to watch: Prime Video

The Fighter director David O. Russell is back with a new movie, based on the life of American football coach and commentator John Madden. Played by Nicolas Cage, Madden follows his life before charting the development of the Madden NFL video game series. Also starring Christian Bale, Kathryn Hahn, and Sienna Miller, there's been relatively little fanfare about the new release, which has received pretty mixed reviews from critics. Still, with such talent involved and an interesting subject, it could be just what you're after for a watch this weekend. It's on Prime Video now.

For more, here's our list of the best movies on Prime Video.

Available: US/UKWhere to watch: Disney Plus

Billed as the show's darkest chapter year, Percy Jackson and the Olympians returns with season 3 on Disney Plus. Starring Walker Scobell once again as Jackson, the series kicks off with a mission gone wrong as the team attempt to rescue Bianca and Nico di Angelo from military school. However, Annabeth Chase gets caught in the crossfire and ends up being captured, leaving Percy and the gang with no choice but to try and find her and stop Atlas' plans. New episodes are dropping weekly on Disney Plus with the first two available now.

Here are our pics of the best shows on Disney Plus.

As we approach awards season next year, expect to start seeing more critically acclaimed movies hitting the streaming platforms. Gentle Monster is Netflix's latest offering starring James Bond actor Léa Seydoux. She plays a concert pianist who leaves her busy life in the city to relocate to the country to help her husband recover from burnout. However, their idyllic new family life soon comes crashing down when police arrive after a horrifying accusation is leveled against her husband. Early reviews praise Seydoux' performance in this tense thriller that explores the chaos inflicted by male predators.

Here's our pick of the best movies on Netflix to watch right now.

Yellowjackets is back for one more spate of episodes tying up all the loose ends in this critically acclaimed story. The premise of the show follows the survivors of a plane crash across two timelines: the immediate aftermath in the '90s and the survivors 25 years later. Teased by its creators as having a "twisted conclusion", the show brings back its main cast including Melanie Lynskey, Christina Ricci, and Sophie Thatcher for the final outing. We can't wait to see how it all pans out.

We've also got a list of the best movies on Paramount Plus.

Netflix is back with a new biographical drama starring Julia Garner. However, her new character couldn't be further away from Anna Sorokin in this story about the rise and fall of the cryptocurrency exchange FTX. Garner plays Caroline Ellison opposite Anthony Boyle's Sam Bankman-Fried of Alameda Research. The Altruists is a tense tale of political machinations, betrayal, and corruption across eight gripping episodes. Critics have been praising Boyle and Garner for their performance in the unpredictable and chaotic true story. All episodes are available to stream now.

If you're one of the countless millions contributing to the collective endangering of global productivity by enjoying Grand Theft Auto 6 at launch, you might have paused in the middle of blatantly disregarding traffic laws to wonder: Wait a second, am I hearing "Weird Al" Yankovic hosting this pretend radio station?

And yes, you are: In a Bluesky post earlier today, the beloved comedic musician and polka maestro confirmed that he offered his voice for DJ Al, who hosts '80s music station Vice City FM alongside Swedish actress, model, and singer Brigitte Nielsen. Their contributions were then double-confirmed by the full GTA 6 credits, which Rockstar published once launch time hit.

I’m the host of GTA 6’s “non-stop ‘80s” radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well! As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!

"I’m the host of GTA 6’s 'non-stop ‘80s' radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well!" Yankovic said. "As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!"

Somewhere out there, Weird Al is securing the love of his virtual latina wife, and I think that's beautiful.

Yankovic is just one of countless recognizable names you'll find if you scroll down the GTA 6 credits. Among the core cast, SNL alumnus Bobby Moynihan voices Cal, Jason's bumbling, conspiracy-brained buddy. The pair's criminal boss man, Brian Heder, is performed by legendary Stephen Root—who you'll likely recognize as Bill Dauterive on King of the Hill, Milton in Office Space, and all kinds of magnificent weirdos across the Coen brothers filmography.

But it's the radio talent where GTA 6's credits get particularly wild. It's a cavalcade of international music icons, comedians, and film figures. While driving around GTA 6, you might hear Lana Del Rey hosting Back Country Radio, or Latin music phenom Bad Bunny on Cocoteo FM. On Dirty South Classics, there's Trina, Trick Daddy, and Gucci Mane. Pop station Flash FM is helmed by Robyn and Alex Consani—the first transgender model to win Model of the Year at the British Fashion Awards and celebrated TikTok goofball. Keith Richards is in there. I didn't even know he was still capable of speech.

On talk radio, you can hear Ted Lasso's Jason Sudeikis, Abbot Elementary's Janelle James, and John Leguizamo of being John Leguizamo fame. Stavros Halkias is on there doing a Conservative talk radio bit. But maybe the most compelling inclusion, for me, is that Kaleidoscope FM is hosted by Jeremy Irons. The Academy Award-winning actor. You were in Kafka, Jeremy. How'd you end up in cyber-Florida?

If I wanted to include all the recognizable names on the list, I'd need a dozen more paragraphs, so I recommend you browse the credits yourself. Or just be content in knowing that Weird Al is waiting for you. That works for me, too.

The 9-1-1 franchise is heating up amid the 2026 TV schedule. While the fall finales of both the Mothership and 9-1-1: Nashville air this week, there's going to be a lot more on the way in the new year. This includes a much-anticipated I Know What You Did Last Summer reunion between Jennifer Love Hewitt and Ryan Phillippe. I'm excited, but what I didn’t expect was Hewitt’s intense take on working with her former co-star again.

Hewitt and Phillippe starred together in the first IKWYDLS film, which was released back in 1997. While Phillippe’s Barry Cox is eventually murdered in the movie, Hewitt’s Julie James becomes the focal point of the sequels. So it’s been close to 30 years since the original movie, and it's great that Barry and Julie are finally back together in some sense.

Following speculation that Phillippe and Hewitt would be reuniting, Hewitt recently confirmed that he would indeed guest star on 9-1-1, reprising his Nashville role as Detective Rogue Kelly. Surprisingly, this is actually the first time that they’ve seen each other since filming wrapped on IKWYDLS, and Hewitt recalled to People just what the atmosphere felt like before the crossover came together. And her take even makes me a bit anxious:

I was so nervous. I had dry mouth and like a full racy heart. Everybody was like, ‘Are you excited?’ I was like, ‘I feel like I’ve forgotten how to act.’ Yeah, it was amazing. We greeted each other with just a big hug and he was like, ‘This is going to be really fun.’ I said, ‘I think it is.’ And it was just, it was a dream.

I love that even though they’ve worked together before, Hewitt can still have those nerves, and I can’t say I blame her. Reuniting with someone you haven’t seen in years -- even if it's on your own turf -- can be intimidating. It sounds like the mood instantly shifted when Phillippe came to set, in a good way, and it makes me even more excited to see how it all turns out.

Phillippe only joined 9-1-1: Nashville for Season 2, so the fact that the two shows are already jumping at the chance to do a crossover featuring him and Hewitt is pretty great. Plus, seeing Phillippe and Hewitt together again is like a '90s-infused dream, and it sounds like they had the time of their lives. Hewitt admitted just how much fun they’ve had from seeing the Internet reacting to the news. She also shared how great it’s been to welcome Phillippe to the 9-1-1 Universe, especially after she reunited with Freddie Prinze Jr. for 2025’s I Know What You Did Last Summer:

He and I have had the best time with people’s reaction. We’ve been DMing going, ‘Did you see it?’ I think we broke the internet. We’ve been having the best time. It was so great because I got to go back and do the movie with Freddie [Prinze Jr.] and sort of have that, and do [our characters] Julie James and Ray again. But this was very different because it was like, [Ryan’s] new in that universe. I’ve been in this universe for a while. It’s such a safe, lovely place to be with the best people. And he and I have not seen each other since I was 18 years old.

As for right now, details surrounding the next 9-1-1 and 9-1-1: Nashville crossover have not been revealed, and I'm eager to see what brings Rogue to Los Angeles. After trying to track down a serial killer in Nashville who is using biblical plagues, hopefully this trip out West will be a bit lighter for him. Of course, if anyone can help him, it’s Hewitt’s Maddie Buckley-Han, who is arguably the best 9-1-1 dispatcher in LA.

Hopefully, crossover information is announced soon, but considering the amount of content Jennifer Love Hewitt has been sharing on her Instagram, she is probably going to keep fans fed for the time being.

For now, viewers can tune in for the fall finales of 9-1-1 and 9-1-1: Nashville, which air this Thursday, November 19, at 8 p.m. ET on ABC, streaming the next day with a Hulu subscription. Both shows will then return from their midseason breaks on Thursday, January 7.

#3747. Infinity Nikki fans threaten to boycott game after promotion by Elon Musk's mother, but there may be a genuine reason for her involvement

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates. Instead, it's because of… Elon Musk's mother.

Some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk. The trailer is for a new update - dubbed Cicia - which adds the ability to drive futuristic hovering cars. The reveal comes days after a widely mocked demonstration of Musk's own Tesla "flying car", which doesn't actually fly.

While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family.

"If they promote Tesla or mention him in the game I'm 100 percent dropping it," wrote one Reddit user (via The Gamer). "Why would they involve that man in a girly fashion game, and if they wanted a car brand partnership why not a Chinese one??!? Infold is addicted to negative attention I swear."

"If Tesla is somehow involved in the design of the car (or worse, an in-game promotion), then I might have to let go," wrote another person in the same thread. "Please please please be wrong."

Though Maye Musk's involvement might seem random, there may be a good explanation for it. "Here's something that might surprise people who only know her as Elon's mother: Maye Musk is a celebrity in China in her own right," Reddit user BarbieSpeedRacer explained.

"She's a successful model, an author, and a recognisable advertising personality. Her memoir became popular with Chinese readers, and she's appeared in campaigns and promotional events for brands including OPPO, Fila, and JNBY."

Her image as "a woman in her seventies who continues to work as a fashion model" is one that resonates with the game's Chinese audience, apparently, especially "among women interested in fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content".

"A Chinese company makes an advertisement featuring a celebrity popular in China, and an international fandom interprets that decision almost exclusively through the lens of American domestic politics," the post added.

So far, calls for a boycott don't appear to have coalesced into a movement, at least judging by the game's subreddit. Even if Western players were to organise one, it's not likely to hurt Infinity Nikki much, as most of the game's revenue - estimated at more than 80 percent - comes from Chinese players.

In Eurogamer's Infinity Nikki review, Jessica Orr said it advances the genre of open-world gacha games and brings competition to rival developer miHoYo, writing: "The changes in length, combat and progression all feel utterly invigorating compared to other Genshin-likes, and it's why Infinity Nikki feels like it could (and should) be on the same trajectory to shake up the gacha scene just like Genshin Impact did in 2020."

For a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer. Yes, if you try to insult XCOM, you're going to get a slap, but we've only just started playing GTA 6 (well, some of us) and we're mostly over the whole 'only runs at 30 fps' thing already.

It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.

GTA 6 certainly does that. That's the impression I get from most members of the team that have played it so far. Though if Rockstar is listening, when you do get around to our precious PC version, we'd love nothing more than 4K60—maybe more.

I will no doubt appreciate frames above 100 fps when GTA 6 comes to PC. Heck, I'd even just appreciate going up to 60 fps. But in my handful of hours with the game thus far, I just have simply not been that bothered by it. Be it smart ways of masking low frames, or even just the slower, methodical control approach of the game, I'm less frustrated with my PS5 running the game at around 30 fps than I was recently playing Phantom Blade Zero at well above 40 fps on a handheld PC.

Maybe that's down to the world having a little bit of magic to it, maybe it's the engrossing tone and atmosphere, maybe it's just because it looks so darn pretty. Maybe it's because I haven't got to the game's most hectic moments yet and haven't really needed to hit a headshot with my console unable to keep up with me. I'll tell you how I'm getting on in another fifty hours. Cool, see you in three days, then?

I was dreading playing GTA 6 on my OG PS5—a dusty ornament that's been chilling out in my living room this last year doing absolutely nothing. I've got a nice gaming PC in my office (RTX 4090, Intel i9 13900K, 32 GB RAM), so it's been a long time since I've had to deal with games dipping below 80 fps. I have been spoiled.

The second I got to control Lucia, my fears seemed justified. Everything just felt sluggish. But that feeling didn't last. I played GTA 6 for around 5 hours last night (I am very tired) and I haven't thought about the frame rate once since that initial section. Whether I'm getting into shootouts with coke smugglers, speeding through the Keys at night, or bouncing around at sea, GTA 6 looks great and feels great.

I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth.

I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth. I'm sure I've encountered drops, but crucially I haven't noticed them. Sure, it's inevitably going to look better and run better on PC, but the lower performance on my PS5 quickly ceased to be an issue, and I'm not regretting playing it on console.

GTA 6 is the kind of game where an uncapped framerate would be nice, but it doesn't feel essential. Like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it—a game I also played at 30 fps before it launched on PC—its pacing is measured. It feels designed around the limitations of the consoles it's launching on, prioritising detail and depth over twitch-based combat and precise interaction. It's exactly what I'd expect from a modern Rockstar game. Also like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it, I still feel the sense of longing for what this game will look like on PC. Make no mistake: the version currently available is a preview for what GTA 6 will be at its best. It's great, but those who can wait will be treated to a superior experience.

It's also possible that the 30 fps cap will feel more restrictive once the online mode arrives—whenever that will be, and in whatever form it takes. It's one thing to handle a lower framerate within Rockstar's meticulously created campaign. It's quite another in a lobby of other players. If GTA 6's multiplayer is even half as chaotic as the current GTA Online, every frame is going to count.

As I was booting up GTA 6, I was expecting to be annoyed by the game's paltry frame rate. And I was—at first. Much like Fraser, during the opening scene with Lucia, I saw my fears come to life on the big screen in front of me. Objects juddering and blurring as I swung my camera around in the cramped cell. Did I just waste £80 on GTA 6 on PS5 when I should've held my nerve for the PC version?

Truth is, the frame rate has had nowhere near as much of a negative impact on my experience while I've been traversing the Floridian wilds as Jason. In part, I think that's because there's a lot more going on, as cars, shops, people, and poultry fly past me as I break most state, federal and ethical laws. That reduces the chance of my eyes fixating on any one object and noticing the adverse effects of the game's lower fps, or the ways Rockstar has gone about covering for it.

Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil.

Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil. That's not just my opinion, that's been scientifically verified (sorta) to be the opinion of PC Gamer readers. Admittedly, some motion blur may be required when the frame rate is this low, so I have played around with a few settings in GTA 6 to find the perfect balance. I'd heard through the grapevine that higher-than-default motion blur (default is 3, goes up to 10) may be preferential to reduce the more obvious juddering that is present at low fps, but whoever says that is no friend of mine. I've landed on setting motion blur to 1 on the standard PS5, as it feels the cleanest overall. I wouldn't blame anyone for turning it off entirely, especially on a more powerful console where the frame rate may not dip as much.

Of course, I do agree with the rest of this lot: in an ideal world, playing the PC version, I'd be pushing a much higher frame rate with motion blur banished to the abyss where it belongs, and a full selection of graphics settings to tinker with to my liking. Yet, to my surprise, I'm not as much of a console version curmudgeon as I thought I'd be.

Is the low frame rate noticeable? Yep. Would it be better at a higher frame rate? Also yep. Is the low frame rate a detriment to my overall enjoyment of GTA 6? Only a smidge.

I don't consider myself much of a framerate snob, but I'll admit I was side-eyeing GTA 6's 30fps just a little bit. Well, that was before the game came out. Now that I have my hands on it, with roughly six hours spent lollygagging around Leonida? I'm hardly noticing it, though I'll most definitely be appreciating a smoother experience once the PC version rolls around.

Like Jacob said, motion blur definitely seems to be masking it somewhat—and I am traditionally a motion blur hater, so it's taken a little getting used to—but I'm genuinely pleasantly surprised at the balance Rockstar has managed to strike between a smooth performance and a dense, rich world.

GTA 6 taught me that I don't much care about frame rates as much as I expected. I got to start playing it a few weeks ago and didn't have anyone to compare notes with, and my first thought was: Huh, they got it to run at 60 fps after all! It all felt very smooth, even when I realized it was 30 fps after all. It was only a bit later I started noticing very occasional drops, like while driving during a gradual lighting chance from day to night.

But that's really infrequent. I think it being consistent is key. I'm on a PS5 Slim, by the way, not a Pro. That's not to say I still can't wait to see it at higher frame rates when it finally gets to PC. But 30 fps feels mostly fine for the time being.

It was actually spending a lot of time playing with handheld gaming PCs and laptops with integrated graphics that reminded me I shouldn't give as much of a shit about frame rate as I do. Largely that obsession is born of having high-end hardware sat in my desktop PC, but when crashing around with a range of handhelds I'm reminded of the old days when 30 fps was a target for PC games, too.

It's also reminded me that it really depends on the game engine, as well. Not every 30 fps game looks the same as other 30 fps games. And Rockstar has obviously worked incredibly hard to make sure that 30 fps looks as good as it possible can. Otherwise why would that be a solid target for all four of the console platforms it's released on?

For the most part Rockstar has done a great job of keeping things smooth.

I've been playing GTA 6 on the Xbox Series X, which does suffer from the odd dip in frame rate, too—though oddly I've only really noticed it during canned animations the characters do starting certain actions, such as opening the trunk of a car or pulling something out of it. But for the most part Rockstar has done a great job of keeping things smooth. And not just by using motion blur. For the record, I'm running that at 0 and have not looked back.

I'm less happy about the vignetting that I'm getting around the darkened edges of the screen, but I'm playing it blown up on a 4K projector so I've got plenty of screen real estate to enjoy. And I have been, thoroughly enjoying it, I mean. The frame rate, for me, hasn't got in the way once.

#3744. You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"

You cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them. This might be a shock to some people, since the option to do so was included in Rockstar games as recently as GTA 5, but here once you've made progress in the story, that's it. Our reviewer confirmed this in his 100+ hour playthrough of the title.

You can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress. By my maths, that means you're going to want to make a new manual save for every 6.6 percent of the game you complete. There is, of course, an auto-save slot, too, that should help you out if you get Busted or Wasted. There will also be key story missions - you will be able to tell when they are, much like you could tell when there was about to be a big heist in GTA 5, a showdown in GTA: San Andreas, or a raid on a gang lord's mansion in GTA: Vice City - that you may want to save before attempting.

It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6. "The team embraced more of an open-ended design philosophy on this project," says David Hynd, vice president of technology on GTA 6. "For example, we really wanted to reduce the number of Mission fails for the player experimenting or trying something different. And we wanted to encourage the player to do what felt right to them for their particular play style."

That means that Rockstar, by considering its deployment of standard gameplay mechanics and enemy AI, and re-evaluating how it approached mission and level design, has created "many different ways" for you to approach any given mission in the game. The result? "It's a lot harder to keep Missions as open as possible (especially in a game as large as this), but the freedom and flexibility it allows the player was worth it," says Hynd. He also notes that the team expects players to "learn and reapply" consistent rules in terms of how the world works - and be surprised when they do and don't apply.

In the previous game, you could access any previous mission you'd completed and be able to play it again on a whim. For GTA 5, you'd simply boot up Story Mode, open the pause menu, go to Game > Replay Mission, and pick the mission you want to play. GTA 6's structure is more complicated, though, hence why Rockstar made the decision to make progress this linear.

#3743. Major Esports Tournament Replaced Caster Commentary With AI Voices And It Went Over Very Poorly

Embark Studios, developer of The Finals and organizer of the game’s Grand Major esports tournament, is facing backlash after replacing human casters with AI voices in a highlight reel. IGN reports that the now-deleted video featured footage from the APAC closed qualifiers, but instead of hearing the human casters that actually called the matches, viewers were treated to AI commentators Scotty and June. The incident is rippling through the esports professional community, with some calling for unionization efforts to protect workers.

Proto, one of the casters replaced in the video, spoke out about the incident on social media.

After 4 cycles, open/closed quals, the time, effort, passion and emotion myself @TheeHyperactive and @bluepanda_casts put in. We get replaced by two Ai casters who even quote us :/ I get they are apart of the game but yikes. Thanks @reachthefinals https://t.co/oC8Zb5GrU0

— Proto / Kai (@ProtoANZ) November 16, 2026

Oscar Lundberg, community and competitive operations lead at Embark Studios, apologized for video on social media. “We intended for Scotty and June to help bring more casual interest into The Finals esports ahead of TGM,” he wrote. “That was the goal, but the work of our talent deserved to be included and highlighted, and it wasnât.”

The writing was on the wall indicating that something like this would happen in The Finals. When it launched in 2023, The Finals was called out by players for its use of AI text-to-speech voice acting, something the devs have acknowledged and embraced. “AI text-to-speech is finally extremely powerful,” said Andreas AlmstrÃ¶m, the game’s audio director in Embark Studios’ “Meet The Makers” podcast. “It gets us far enough in terms of quality and allows us to be extremely reactive to new ideas.” Earlier this year, The Finals released Dynamic Commentary, a feature that allows the AI commentator to call out players by name whenever something happens during a match.

Dynamic Commentary is the new feature that will earn you praise from your favorite commentator Scotty, coming in PRIME TIME on Oct. 20!

Live commentary in a live match for the play you just pulled. Now this is what a Game Show is all about!â¦ pic.twitter.com/8acAZGY2Zw

— THE FINALS (@reachthefinals) October 18, 2026

It stands to reason that if a developer is comfortable with using AI-text-to-speech to power the game’s in-universe equivalent of esports casting, they might extend that beyond the confines of the game, possibly to see if anyone would notice or care enough about it. Having in-game AI commentary is the inch, this video experiment is the mile. Thankfully esports professionals, many of whom have lost their jobs over the last six years as studio interest and investment has declined, didn’t let this go by unremarked.

In an interview with IGN, Proto spoke about potential organization efforts to prevent something like this from taking hold in the esports community. “I think industry wide, we definitely need to implement some kind of protection for commentary teams as well as production teams,” he said. “You got to protect those people’s jobs.”

After releasing five projects on the 2026 movie schedule, Anne Hathaway disappeared in a plume of smoke (as she joked she would) and finally got some time off. However, not long after she finished her generational press run, she had her third baby. Now, we know the gender of her little one; however, it’s because The Devil Wears Prada 2 costume designer seemingly leaked it.

Molly Rogers, who worked on the fairly well-reviewed The Devil Wears Prada sequel, took to her Instagram story to congratulate Hathaway and her baby. She did so by posting a cute photo of a bear wearing a fun patchwork dress and bucket hat (which emulates a look the actress wore in The Devil Wears Prada 2). She also revealed the gender of the actress’s baby. Take a look:

News broke on November 17 that Hathaway had given birth, after she was spotted walking in New York City with her little one strapped to her chest. She announced he was pregnant with her third child in June, and she promoted The Odyssey, The End of Oak Street and Verity after that. So, we got to see some gorgeous looks featuring her bump, and then, a little over a month after Verity came out, it was revealed that she’d given birth.

Now, we know her baby’s gender too. It’s unclear if the actress was aware of Rogers post or if the designer did it on purpose. However, no matter how you shake it, the gender of Hathaway’s baby was seemingly leaked when Rogers wrote:

Congrats are in order for proud mama [Anne Hathaway] & her new addition to family….a baby girl!

At the time of this writing, Hathaway has not posted about giving birth. In fact, since she vanished in a plume of smoke, she’s only posted twice – once on October 27 to promote Verity’s VOD release (which was filmed when they made the movie) and another time on November 12 to wish Ryan Gosling a happy birthday (they share the same birthday, by the way). So, it’s unclear how she’d feel about this information regarding her baby’s gender being public knowledge.

It is wonderful to know she reportedly had a little girl, though. Hathaway and her husband, Adam Shulman, have two sons as well; their first boy, Jonathan, was born in 2016, and the second, Jack, was born in 2019. We don’t know the name of baby No. 3 yet. However, if I had to guess, I think there’s reason to believe this little girl’s name starts with a J.

Hopefully, that news will be shared when Anne Hathaway and her family are ready to do so. In the meantime, you can stream The Devil Wears Prada 2 with a Disney+ subscription right now.

I've been playing GTA 6 through the morning to try to see what the fuss is about, and now I totally get it. After mere hours in the game, I'm already coming to terms with the scale of it; not just the size of the map, but the attention to detail on every object and interaction. But I have to remind myself, this is sure to be the worst version of GTA 6 we'll ever play.

That sounds like an insult, but I mean the exact opposite. If this is where the game is at launch, at its most barebones, running on years-old consoles on their way out, then think of what it will be like at its peak.

I work for PC Gamer, so forgive my snobbery when I say the PC version should be far superior to what we're currently playing on consoles.

A part of that is the possible frame rate bump from running on modern PC hardware. The standard PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X are powered by pretty outdated architectures by today's standards: RDNA 2 and Zen 2. You're looking at the Radeon RX 6000 series and Ryzen 3000 series for PC equivalents.

These chips have recently received support for more modern ML-powered FSR upscaling techniques from AMD, though Rockstar has only seen fit to enable FSR 4 on the Xbox Series S to help the underpowered console along. Sony also has AMD-powered upscaling tech for the PS5 Pro, but the standard PS5 doesn't get a whiff of that.

It's only really the PS5 Pro with a more modern GPU—loosely equivalent to an RX 7800 XT—that might temper expectations for how fast the game may run on a modern gaming PC. Rockstar has said the PlayStation 5 Pro wouldn't be capable of a steady 60 fps even with the more powerful hardware compared to the base model; however, hints at the sluggish CPU as perhaps the weak link. The PS5 Pro runs the same old eight-core CPU as the standard PS5, and if Rockstar's engine can make use of faster, more multithreaded CPUs with lots of cache, we should see a performance bump on PC.

That's not to exclude older gaming PCs. The Xbox Series S can cope with GTA 6, so should many gaming PCs of all levels. Notably so if Rockstar offers a range of upscaling options.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It's ubiquitous upscaling that should make an even bigger difference to an eventual PC release and performance on all manner of PC. We know the game supports FSR 4.1, as both Sony and Microsoft are already using this as the foundation for their upscaling technologies on console, and Red Dead Redemption 2 offers both FSR and DLSS on PC. Since that game's release, we've seen the advent of frame generation technologies from both AMD and Nvidia, which could further increase how smooth GTA 6 feels on PC.

As a serial settings tweaker, I've been sorely disappointed by the sliders, or lack thereof, available to me in GTA 6 on the base PS5. I want levels to this stuff; an advanced menu for advanced men like me. I want to manage the foliage detail, draw distance, and ray-traced effects. Speaking of which, I'm sure we'll have the option to enable ray-traced shadows, currently exclusive to the PS5 Pro, and crank up the quality of most effects in the game on PC.

The non-RT shadows are one of the few noticeable drawbacks about the standard PS5 version of GTA 6 I'm currently playing. They can pop in and out from reflections, and there is a jagginess to them in places.

Is any game going to be modded more than GTA 6? Our Joshua has been busy modding GTA 5 to try to turn it alchemy-like into GTA 6 for months now, and he never ran out of mods to install. While he may have strayed from his original mission almost immediately, the message is clear: GTA 6 is going to have a seriously busy mod scene.

The game will be all the better for it, too. Not every mod is going to enable a roving band of militant furries (Joshua's words, and no need to mod those into GTA 6) or trap the player in a tiny car; I'm sure GTA 6 will actually be a better game for the efforts of modders. It just takes a PC version and some intrepid people to make it happen.

This one is easy; one of the reasons for GTA 5's long-lasting legacy is the combination of GTA Online and custom jobs via the creator. Neither of which are actually here for GTA 6 yet. So on a very basic level, and you don't have to be a PC gamer to agree on this point, GTA 6 is going to get a lot better for the eventual online mode. And there will be an online mode, right? Even if Rockstar hasn't technically announced one is on the way yet.

On the flipside, if you're constantly getting griefed by a guy that only plays GTA 6 all day and won't let you leave your house in GTA Online, perhaps you could argue the game was better when it was single-player only.

It pains me to admit it, but GTA 6 is not only going to eventually run better on PC. It might be the definitive version in my eyes, but console gamers do have a high-fidelity future ahead of them, too. Both Sony and Microsoft are planning new consoles that seem pretty likely to come out in roughly a year's time—providing the memory crisis doesn't ruin everything—and AMD is set to be providing more powerful silicon for these systems.

We're expecting to see the RDNA 5 architecture make its way into the next-gen consoles, paired with Zen 6 CPU cores of some size and description (these may be heterogeneous). That would put the consoles on a level playing field with PC components likely to launch around the same time (Zen 6 should be available on desktop by then, while perhaps a more limited launch for RDNA 5 by early 2028).

So that whole spiel about how current-gen consoles are years behind our fancy PCs won't get me so far once these new systems come out. I'll have to find a new stick to bash consoles with… er, not enough RGB LEDs? Anyways, the definitive GTA 6 experience on console is still yet to come—that'll be the version that's ready to make the most of these more capable units sometime next year or in 2028.

There are going to be a helluva lot of patches, upgrades, and DLCs to come for GTA 6. Remember, GTA V got a new first-person mode with the then-next-gen PS4 and Xbox One, so there's plenty of opportunity for genuine upgrades down the line.

Though, saying that, by recent PC standards (poor ports, game-breaking bugs, and more), this GTA 6 launch has been relatively issue-free. I mean, I've seen a couple of visual glitches and my colleagues have had some strange men falling out of the sky, but besides those open-world oddities you may expect of a game of this size and stature, it's been pretty smooth sailing so far.

I just hope the PC version can claim a similarly clean sweep for its eventual launch. So far, no word on when that might be.

#3740. CNN Calls GTA 6 The ‘Most Intense Version Of Pac-Man‘

Folks, I’m not sure if you are aware of this, but video games, like Grand Theft Auto 6, have come a long way since Pac-Man. I’m aware of that, but perhaps the people at CNN might want to play a video game made in the last 20 years.

Today, on CNN, three adults who are paid money to report on the events of the world were asked to talk about the just-launched Grand Theft Auto 6 for a bit, and it was extremely embarrassing and sad for all involved. For some reason, in an effort to explain what GTA 6 is to people who aren’t big gamers, they decided to compare it to Pac-Man. Seriously.

"… think of it as the most intense version of Pac-Man…" – CNN on GTA VI

Come on, man. This industry made over 200 Billion dollars in revenue last year alone. What are we doing here?

— Raj Patel (@rajio.bsky.social) 2026-11-19T21:36:55.884Z

“If you’re not a gamer, think of it as the most intense version of Pac-Man where you are being chased, and you’re chasing with the most lifelike graphics possible.”

Wow! What a terrible way to describe GTA 6. Or really any popular video game made in the last 20 years. Look, I’m not suggesting these people need to be gaming experts. But video games aren’t a tiny niche only played by kids down at the arcade. They’re a massively popular, successful, and influential medium. Some of the biggest shows and movies of the last few years are direct adaptations of games like The Last of Us and Fallout. And GTA 6 is the biggest of the big. You could maybe not waste everyone’s time with such a lazy and useless description.

It’s also just weird because most people on this planet have a basic understanding of what GTA is in 2026. It’s that game where you steal cars and run around and shoot cops. That’s not a perfect description, but it’s much better than the crap CNN is sharing on the air when the network is suddenly forced to talk about video games due to a really, really big one dropping.

Anyway, I can’t wait to be in my 70s and hear reporters in the mainstream media describe GTA 12 or whatever as the best version of Pac-Man you’ve ever seen. Video games really have come a long way, folks…

SPOILERS ahead for Eternally Yours, now streaming with a Paramount+ subscription, with new episodes dropping on Thursdays.

I knew Eternally Yours would be one of my favorite new shows on the 2026 TV schedule ever since it premiered, but in the past few weeks, my love for the show has doubled. And that’s all to do with the impressive amount of exciting setups I’m seeing from the comedy. It’s also so nice to have a new vampire family to follow after all my Twilight rewatches.

Given Eternally Yours is a half-hour comedy, you’d think it wouldn’t lean into a larger storyline until later on, but the fact that it does makes me feel confident about the quality and longevity of the series from the creators of Ghosts. Let’s talk about three big developments that I think are being laid out already in Season One.

New comedies can be difficult to get on board with early because oftentimes they need some time to settle in, and not every network or streaming service is willing to bet on them. Eternally Yours has been killing it with its Season One rollout, and is expected to be renewed (per TV Insider). One plotline that has me excited to tune in for more episodes is what happened in Episode 4, “Halloween”.

In the episode from a couple of weeks ago, we learn about something called the Wolfsbane Chalice, which the vampire coven has been in possession of for many years. Basically, it helps protect them from werewolf attacks. While most of the episode revolves around some of the coven thinking Max allowed it to be lost, it was Phyllis who used it for a special Halloween drink and accidentally broke it. I’m convinced this is setting up a confrontation with werewolves, and it’s not the only clue so far.

That brings me to Episode 6, “Eternal Sunshine of Phyllis’s Mind,” where I think two developments that will have a payoff later came up. The first is the flashback for Emma, where we learn that she had a werewolf stalker named Larry who killed off a number of her boyfriends. Between the loss of the Wolfsbane Chalice and this story, I’m convinced either the finale or an episode down the line will see the return of Larry in the present day, who comes out to get Emma’s new man, Max.

The final setup, which is definitely my favorite, also comes from last week’s episode. Phyllis is one of the best parts of Eternally Yours so far, but I was curious if they would address how messed up it is that her memories are always being wiped.

Thankfully, “Eternal Sunshine of Phyllis’s Mind” not only brought it up, but it seemingly fixed the problem when Jesse decides to tell his wife he’s a vampire at the end of the episode. While I thought Phyllis not knowing she’s in a vampire coven would last for a while, now that it’s not, I’m actually so excited about what happens next.

It’s going to be hilarious to watch as Phyllis unpacks the secret world she lives in, and I’ll be curious if she decides whether she wants to be a vampire, too. I also wonder if her finding out will also create more problems for the coven, like her accidentally telling a werewolf?

I’m honestly so astonished at how many exciting plot lines Eternally Yours has been setting up in just six episodes, and I can’t wait for the rest of the season.

#3738. Just how detailed is the audio in GTA 6? Well, even convenience store refrigerators "all have their own unique sounds", says Rockstar dev

If you've been online at all today, you'll know that what feels like the entire world is currently fawning over GTA 6. As the reviews dropped, one thing quickly became very clear: this is a game absolutely packed with detail. Our own Chris noted that, thanks to this focus on specific detail and unbelievable nuance, Grand Theft Auto 6 is "the most unbelievable video game world ever made". And it's no accident: this is something Rockstar put a lot of dedicated effort into.

It's been well-established that the studio has gone above and beyond to make this interactive world one of the most richly-developed we've ever seen: Rockstar has told us it "re-engineered" its weather systems to "achieve a sense of scale we haven't felt before," adding hurricanes, rainbows and heavy rain. It simulated and built a complex drug system, allowing Lucia and Jason to partake in drug use "directly from their inventory" and "at any time". But there are still details emerging from the dev team that are blowing my mind. And the most recent byte of information I saw was related to how Rockstar worked with sound.

"Much of the dynamic soundscape is informed by the incredibly detailed art throughout the world," explains Alastair MacGregor, vice president of audio at Rockstar. "One small example is that convenience store refrigerators all have their own unique sounds. In a run-down store, the refrigerators and freezers are loud and sound like they are badly maintained. Their compressor units can be heard mechanically whirring away from years of neglect. As a result, the bottles behind the doors can be heard shaking and the units click on and off more frequently. In an up-market store, the refrigerators are quieter, adding a subtle hum to the environment."

This level of detail is, quite frankly, absurd. It's a testament to granularity Rockstar is willing to go to in making Leonida feel truly lived-in and realistic. And this level of production isn't restricted to internal locations, either. "On the ambient side, we love the contrast between the manicured luxury islands, with the sizzle of crickets and lawn sprinklers backed by birdsong, yacht halyards clanging in the distance, and yard work going on, versus urban areas with the sounds of people living on top of each other - snatches of every genre of music, distant voices, cars peeling out, construction, the omnipresent hum of elderly air conditioners struggling with the humidity," continues MacGregor.

He goes on to say that if you're wandering the streets of Gellhorn - a coastal city in Kelly County on the western side of Leonida - it's acoustically a very different vibe than the high-rise centre of Vice City, where the sound bounces between the buildings. This means that the engine is handling not just the sounds of things as minute as bugs in the grass, but also how that sound travels, and interacts with other physical entities in the world. "We've spent years iterating on reverb technology to make sure that you can feel that - from the pops of cars backfiring to the wash of a helicopter passing by overhead to birds squawking in the trees," concludes MacGregor.

GTA 6 launches tomorrow - Thursday, 19th November - for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It's also worth noting that Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week.

In a distressing update on Steam Machine stock and pricing, Valve says "we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them" as the RAM and storage markets remain crunched.

"We've been able to fulfill all current reservations for the 512GB model with no waitlist remaining, and have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders," Valve says in a new Steam post.

Here comes the other shoe: "However, we are continuing to encounter supply constraints for hardware components, which impacts our ability to source parts."

512GB Steam Machines can be purchased directly "while supplies last," Valve says, but once the current stock runs dry, the company will "flip it to out-of-stock rather than begin building another waitlist."

The 2TB model is in worse shape. While Valve has "finished getting purchases invites out to all reservation holders," nobody still on the waitlist is "guaranteed a unit." However, Valve says everyone on the waitlist "will retain their position in line."

That waitlist is now being closed, however, as "there are more people on the waitlist than units available." As a result, the 2TB Steam Machine will also show as out-of-stock in the store.

"You are welcome to choose to purchase a 512GB model instead (while supplies last)," Valve says. But you will have to leave the 2TB waitlist to do that.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them," Valve admits. "The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained."

Valve expects to have "more information" come January, but I wouldn't bet on good news, as the RAM and storage drought is projected to continue well beyond January amid AI data center fever.

It's a rare sight for PlayStation Studios, which has secured a Game of the Year nomination every year since 2015.

PlayStation has published several games this year that might usually be shoe-ins for a Game of the Year nomination. Despite missing out on the Game of the Year slot, however, PlayStation still features in other categories. All three of the aforementioned games are up for various, non-GOTY awards, while Marathon is nominated for Best Multiplayer, and the upcoming God of War Laufey for Most Anticipated. #3735. GTA 6 Is Even Better When You Play It Side-By-Side With Your Wife

Needless to say, there are lots of people out there currently playing Grand Theft Auto 6, and despite what a lot of headlines and social media jokes insist, itâs not solely a boysâ club. Perhaps more than any other GTA game before it, the latest title attracts all kinds of people, and some of these people happen to be couples living in the same houseâmirroring GTA 6âs protagonists just a little bit.

My partner, who has not played a Grand Theft Auto game before, and I have both been excited to lay our hands on GTA 6, and stayed up late last night for the midnight unlock time. But unlike most in our situation, we neither passed the controller back and forth nor went to different rooms to enjoy our games separately. See, because I am an insane person, I have a setup that lets us both start the game simultaneously.

Obviously, both my partner and I are game journalists, and both of us have worked in this industry for many years. When we first started living together, after she moved to San Francisco to join IGN, I foresaw a situation in which we would both have to review games at the same time. Maybe, then, it would make sense for us to have setups that allowed us to play different consoles simultaneously, maybe in different rooms or parts of the same room.

âWhy not just put them next to each other?â she posited as we mentally planned out our apartment. Why not, indeed!

That birthed what visiting friends all point out is a truly odd setup, but one that occasionally pays dividends. In the setup, we have my TV on the left and her TV on the right. The consoles on the left side are mine and only hook into my TV, while the consoles on the right side do the same to her TV, with the PC in the middle duplicating the image to both. Usually one person will wear headphones if weâre both playing something.

This works out well with a lot of games. When we were playing through Elden Ring before release side-by-side, one of us would occasionally look at the other’s screen, not recognize where the other person was, and so weâd share notes on how to get there. When Tears of the Kingdom launched at midnight, an informal race to get all the shrines motivated us to solve puzzles in more interesting ways than the other person.

With Grand Theft Auto 6, though, it allowed us to see exactly what little details were changing in the game depending on our different actions and approaches.

In the gameâs prologue, Lucia tries her best to make it back to a coffee shop while the police search for her, scouring the city block. Since itâs mere minutes after the opening of the game, my partner and I got there at roughly the same time. She, pragmatic as she is, chose to walk along the sidewalks until the cops eventually picked her up. I tried to cut around the building and swim, and then I got hit in the head by a police boat and was knocked unconscious. Whoops.

For me, in the cutscene that followed, Lucia was being handcuffed to a gurney while EMS and police pushed her into the back of an ambulance. For my partner, Lucia was being manhandled by police into the back of a cop car. In both situations, she pleaded about needing to go back to the coffee shop, but it was maybe a bit more fraught and scary in my case as she fought to maintain consciousness.Â

The scenes were similar, but different, and it was fascinating to be able to watch them side-by-side like this. That wow factor has kind of kept up throughout as we’ve continued playing. In an early mission, I watched her, playing as Jason, enter a car impound lot in a completely different way than I had. She gave me tips about when I would be able to play as Lucia, noticing that I was bumming around a lot (to which I answered, âBut I have to make sure sheâs happy with the house first.â)Â

I wonder if Iâm signing up for a lifetime of doing more chores without realizing it.

We’re planning to play the bulk of the rest of the game like this; it probably won’t surprise anyone that we have a lot of TVs around the house and sometimes I move consoles around to play things in my office. But our setup is interesting, and it lets us spend time together while still partaking in hobbies that we love. Tonight weâre both going to continue playing GTA while I set up a laptop on the coffee table to watch the episode of AEW Dynamite that we missed yesterday, and that might be pushing it a little bit. Or maybe three screens is the perfect number?

Florence Pugh seems to be everywhere these days, from starring in two of the biggest 2026 movies of the year Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three to headlining Netflix's must-watch series, East of Eden. Unfortunately, the more eyes on someone, its often the more scrutiny that follows. With that, Pugh just got real the upsetting discourse she's been seeing about her body as of late.

Pugh went viral this past Tuesday for commenting on an Instagram post speaking about how people are apparently noticing changes in her face shape lately. The Oscar nominee wrote "sadly puppy fluff doesn't last forever" after sharing distress about people not being able to tell the difference between aging and surgery. Now, Pugh has decided to open up further on all the talk about her. In her words:

I woke up the other morning and quite a lot of you were discussing my face and body in such a disturbing way. I learnt online that I had been on Ozempic? I learnt that I'd had upper bleph? Lower bleph? Filler? Face lipo? Bucal fat remover? Chin surgery? Nose surgery?! What the fucking hell guys, I didn't even know that one person COULD get all of these things done over night if they wanted to? Yes, I'm disturbed.

Pugh has been a longtime advocate for body positivity and rarely ever minces words on the subject. The actress has spoken out about how she's been asked to diet for roles and fired back about comments about her body on the internet and Hollywood double standards before. This time, she spoke specifically to a growing trend online that sees people comparing photos of women and speculating whether they've gotten any plastic surgery done. Pugh cleared things up, saying this:

I have never been on Ozempic. I have NEVER done any face surgery. And don't EVER say that I didn't make my own nose, I've always had that beautiful ski slope. Even as a baby!

Not that she owed anyone an explanation! Because Pugh has been "spent [her] whole career defending and protecting bodies that just grow the way they grow" it sounds like she couldn't stand all the discussion, especially around her trademark nose. Pugh even posted this on her Instagram story to prove the point:

Florence Pugh went on to say that her body perhaps looks different this year because when she started the year, she had two New Year's Resolutions: to change her relationship with alcohol and be able to do at least one pull up at the gym. And guess what, she's been working with a trainer all year, and she's able to do it now. As she showed off:

Pugh can now do six pulls ups and lift 243 pounds! She said the accomplishment is "everything" to her and she "worked so hard" to get there before saying she's "looking after [herself], and that's literally it."

The East of Eden star also took the opportunity to say that thanks to her goals she put into action, this year has had "the opportunity to be rested, to sleep, to wake up and work out and eat regularly and healthily". She also got real that through her journey she's only lost two pounds, because she's been focusing mainly on gaining muscle. Her recent health journey comes after years of online bullying from social media users. As she wrote:

I also want to point out that over the years I have been in the public eye, I have received comments or messages daily about how I look like a pig, that I'm fat and should go on a run, that I shouldn't be proud of my body, that I SHOULD go on Ozempic, that I shouldn't show my midrift because I shouldn't be proud of it.

Pugh remarked that on one occasion, the size of her thighs were even pointed out in a movie review. But, there's more. The 30-year-old also revealed that she had to sue a few publications this year for buying AI pictures of her getting injectables and published them as "real images". Check out the full message below:

A post shared by Florence Pugh (@florencepugh)

These days, as there's a lot of changing body norms in the media, partially propelled by the rise of GLP-1s , Florence Pugh continues to fight for loving bodies as they are in her latest social media post. You can see her in both Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three on December 18.

#3733. GTA 6 breaks the all-time livestream viewer record hours before it's available to play for most of the world

Hours before it's even playable in most of the world, Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken the record for the most viewers across livestreaming platforms like Twitch.

According to streaming data and analytics website Streams Charts, GTA 6 had amassed 6.38m live viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick at 12:30 UTC today. At that time, the game had been officially available for a few hours in New Zealand, and elsewhere by using a region-switch trick.

The previous record for most live viewers was set by Valorant, Riot Game's popular tactical shooter, during its closed beta in xx. That game brought in 1.74m live viewers, but it's worth noting there was a promotion offering players a chance to access the beta if they watched a stream. Despite having no such incentive, GTA 6 has more than tripled Valorant's record.

Twitch is the largest platform for GTA 6 streams according to Streams Charts, and already the game is the 6th biggest category in Twitch history. It's also expected the figure will increase as GTA 6 launches officially in more regions of the world.

If you'd like to find out when exactly Grand Theft Auto 6 releases for you, check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 launch time guide for an accurate list by country. You can also read the Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 guide for a full breakdown on all the details ahead of its launch in your region.

GTA 6 seems to be a technical miracle with very little complaints about performance outside of its pitiful 30fps, but it seems something's going on with the PS5 version of the game that's causing repeated crashes.

Many Reddit users are reporting crashes mid-game associated with the PS5 error code CE-108225-1, which seems to repeat itself after certain story moments early in the game, preventing players from moving forward. We were able to quickly dig out more than a dozen Reddit posts from people seemingly experiencing a very similar, game-breaking crash: "Legit cannot get past opening cut scene tried so many different things. Game just keeps crashing with same error code. I skipped cutscene and it just froze after as well," reads one such report.

"Ive tried everything. Cleared cache, rebuilt database, reinstalled, updated, restored license and it does the same thing," says another disgruntled Redditor. "Paid $100 for a game I can’t play."

The error seems to be affecting GTA 6 players on base and digital or Slim PS5 models, and appears to be specifically related to GTA 6 as I can't find any recent reports connected to other games. Some Redditors have drawn up extensive lists of attempted solutions, but so far there doesn't seem to be any that are successful.

A reasonable next step would be to check Rockstar's ever-reliable support page for a solution, but the recently updated guidance on error troubleshooting just directs to the official support pages for Xbox and PlayStation, and under the heading "How to fix error code CE-108225-1," Sony gives some laughably useless advice: "Try updating your game," and if that doesn't work, "please visit PlayStation Repairs."

Unfortunately, there are no updates to download for GTA 6 yet, and one Redditor who contacted Sony's repair service said they were quoted £300, which really doesn't seem like a very favorable outcome.

While there are enough reports out there to warrant a response from Rockstar and/or Sony, GTA 6 players on PS5 shouldn't panic just yet. A smattering of error codes on social media doesn't necessarily mean this is a super widespread issues, even though I'd be lying if I said I wasn't a little nervous as a PS5 players myself who has so far, thankfully, experienced zero crashes in my several hours with the game. Regardless, I've reached out to Sony for comment and will update this article if I hear back.

Ubisoft Montreal and Quebec are the latest to fall under the axe.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Ubisoft has laid off 166 people from its offices in Montreal and Quebec City, saying in a statement provided to PC Gamer that its "production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."

Founded in 1997, Ubisoft Montreal is one of the biggest game studios in the world, with roughly 4,000 employees as of 2022. Ubisoft Quebec, launched in 2005, is somewhat smaller but still substantial: Its website says the studio has "a team of over 600 creative, passionate, and innovative talents." The cuts reportedly impact employees who could not be assigned elsewhere after their existing projects were cancelled or rescoped.

Whatever the reason, it's bleak: This is the latest round in a series of layoffs that have battered the company since it announced a major restructuring in January, which followed years of struggles including workplace misconduct scandals, persistent difficulties getting games launched, and underperformance among big releases. Ubisoft said in today's half-year financial report report that it's reduced its headcount by roughly 1,100 people over the past six months.

Ubisoft did have a significant hit earlier this year with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, but that wasn't enough to prevent post-launch layoffs at developer Ubisoft Singapore. Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot said today that "Q2 exceeded our expectations, driven by the continued success of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and solid contributions from our broader portfolio."

Warning! The following contains spoilers for the The Circle series premiere on Hulu "Welcome To The Circle." Stream it with a Hulu subscription, or read at your own risk!

The Circle's Hulu premiere dropped this past Tuesday, and it was mostly what I hoped it would be. For starters, I was right that adding celebrities to the mix made the start of the season even better to watch. That said, there is one thing I really miss in comparison to the long-running version I enjoyed with my Netflix subscription, but I'm willing to continue watching despite that.

Michelle Buteau served as The Circle's host for all of its original run on Netflix, but as we knew ahead of its premiere on the 2026 TV schedule, she wasn't invited for this new installment. I didn't think it would be a big deal before watching the premiere, but I have to admit, I really miss her.

Buteau, who readers may know from her Netflix series Survival of the Thickest, was more than just a narrator for The Circle. She brought a lot of comedy to the game, which I felt was a little lacking in Hulu's premiere. Buteau's personality helped shape the tone of the show, which helped make it one of the best reality series.

During the premiere, I couldn't help but feel like I was watching American Idol without Ryan Seacrest. That feels like a problem, because while Hulu clearly felt The Circle needed retooling for its new era, the show lasted seven seasons for a reason. Again, I still enjoyed the episode, but there was no denying that there was a definite shift in tone due to the comic's absence.

It may just take time for me to get used to Tinx (Christina Najjar), who comes into The Circle with plenty of experience elsewhere. Before she was hosting the Hulu series, the influencer rose to fame through her no-nonsense advice. This evolved into a podcast, a New York Times best-selling book and a deal with SiriusXM.

I Can't Stop Thinking About The Circle's AI Twist And I Have So Many Feelings

Tinx has the resume for the role, but one episode in, I don't really see the same personality in her that I saw in Michelle Buteau. Granted, it's been one episode, and if we were all judged by our first day on the job, many of us would probably in trouble.

Nevertheless, the role of host on The Circle is very critical, so I hope I get used to it sooner rather than later. There's already so much happening after the first episode, and we need someone who can navigate all the craziness that will unfold over these next few weeks before the $100,000 winner is crowned.

Catch new episodes of The Circle on Hulu on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays at 9:00 p.m. ET. I'm eager to see this new format in action, and I'm ready for an audience vote to really shake things up as we get underway!

#3729. GTA 6 is so big, it managed to break Reddit - and it isn't even actually out yet

Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't even out yet, and it's already causing some technical issues over at the game's official Reddit page.

In a post verified by r/GTA6 moderators and pinned to the page, user and moderator PapaXah wrote "GTA 6 broke Reddit", and explained that "many things" were currently busted at the time of the post. Looking through Reddit, many flairs (little labels attached to posts) aren't loading properly and appear as a string of code rather than proper images. PapaXah also replied to one user suggesting they make real flairs based on these busted flairs, writing: "Reddit's so broken I couldn't even do it. We actually have a bunch of new flairs that I can't even upload."

Another moderator, TekS, also acknowledged that some user's posts may not be viewable as a result of ongoing strain on Reddit during GTA 6's release. They commented: "If you can't post/comment or see your user flair, well, know that it's perfectly normal."

Ahead of the game's full launch across the world, the Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken viewership records across streaming platforms like Twitch and YouTube. Interesting details about the game are also trickling out, including the fact that different refrigerators have their own unique sounds. Video games, ladies and gentlemen.

With Grand Theft Auto 6 releasing today, our review has been released to the wild with it. It is overwhelmingly positive, with Chris Tapsell dubbing GTA 6 as "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made" and rated it a full five stars.

I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

It is time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5. Did we not say goodbye literally yesterday, when I installed a mod named Farewell Los Santos, and there was even a video and everything, and we put Komm Susser Tod over it?

No. 53 mods ago, I told you, the reader, that my mission here was to either mod GTA 5 into a version of Grand Theft Auto 6 on PC, or break the game trying. Admittedly, my mission was successful: GTA 5 is actually better than GTA 6 now. But that means only one thing: as a final send-off, I can think of nothing better to do than finally fulfil the other potential outcome of our initial gambit. It is time to break GTA 5 entirely.

I have installed Fences Network, Simple Weapons Saving, Dragon Trainer V – How to Train Your Dragon Mega Pack, Empire: Singleplayer Overhaul, In The Hood (Gang), BodyGuard Menu, Addon Car Spawner Plus, Rideable Sandworm, Buckme Money App, Realistic Tactical Loadout - GTA VI Inspired Visible Weapon Carry, Pickup, & HUD System [Legacy & Enhanced], Gang Mod Respect System, Los Santos Collapse [Legacy & Enhanced] Zombie mod, The Last Heist - An ending for GTA V [Story Mod | 10 Missions], Real Life Mod [Legacy], Raul's Revenge DLC, Warzone Infil, RageHandlingEditor (RHE) [Legacy & Enhanced], On foot radio (with animations and headphones customization), Keep Right, and Ending C with M83 Midnight City.

In other words, everything that was on the front page of GTA 5 Mods dot com's scripts section when I loaded it up this morning. This took some doing, involving quite a lot of faffing around with OpenIV and myriad .rpf packages to get everything installed.

Would you be surprised to hear (you will not be surprised to hear) the game does not start anymore? GTA 5 has gone to that great sleep that awaits us all. Oh, don't get me wrong: it will boot to the main menu, but try to resume a game or start a new one and GTA 5 will, valiantly, spend about a minute and a half with its cogs audibly grinding against another before simply dumping you back at your desktop—no fanfare, no error message, just swift death. After enduring 53 other mods without completely breaking, it rests now in the great beyond.

The open-world RPG saw a significant bump over the summer

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Christopher Nolan's hit summer film The Odyssey drove a big boost in sales for Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed Odyssey, an open-world action RPG that shares the Greek setting.

In its latest financial report, Ubisoft tips its hat to "a major summer movie" without calling out Nolan by name.

"The rest of the Assassin’s Creed catalog also performed strongly, supported by effective promotional campaigns," the company says. "Assassin’s Creed Odyssey also materially benefited from the release of a major summer movie and more recently Assassin’s Creed Valhalla passed the 40 million players threshold. The franchise will celebrate its 20th anniversary next year. This is a major milestone for the brand, which is preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and community moments."

Assassin's Creed Odyssey players and analysts observed as much back in July, with Alinea Analytics reporting a 90% jump in player engagement following Nolan's blockbuster. Ubisoft's backlog is impressively active in general, but we were seeing pretty rare figures for an eight-year-old single-player game. Odyssey even emerged as the highest-rated game in the series on Steam on the back of the summer bump.

If you're looking for a playable version of The Odyssey, you won't find a strict adaptation in Ubisoft's riff, but you could certainly do worse. For an irresponsibly large Greek sandbox, Assassin's Creed Odyssey fits the bill.

Here's what we said in 2018 in our 5/5 Assassin's Creed Odyssey review: "No-one's made an open-world RPG with this much depth and brilliance since The Witcher 3."
